mainTopic: A minor's deposit and deathbed claims, חזקה between father and son, and the brother who ran the family business
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about deposits from people who are not fully independent. A deposit from a קטן is put into a safe investment for him and goes to his heirs if he dies. If any of these depositors says before dying that the item belongs to someone else, we follow it only if it is believable. רב applies this to the rings of רבה בר בר חנה's wife, and the גמרא gives two versions of his test. The גמרא then explains that a 'סגולה' is either a ספר תורה or a fruit-bearing date palm. Next, רב יוסף and רבא argue whether a father and son who split their finances can make a חזקה on each other's property, and the הלכה follows רבא that they can. Finally, רב and שמואל argue about a brother who ran the family business and claims the assets came from his mother's father. רב פפא challenges שמואל's claim that רב agrees once that brother has died, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A deposit from a minor is invested safely for him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a guardian who took a deposit from a קטן must invest it safely for him, and if the קטן dies, give it to his heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone took a deposit from a minor, he should invest it safely for him. If the minor dies, he must return it to the minor's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the rule for a deposit taken from a קטן. You can't just hand it back to a child, so it must be kept safe in a protected investment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in this ברייתא there were rules for a woman and a slave, where the item is given back to them, or to the husband or master if they die. A קטן is different: he cannot look after property, so the guardian must set it up as a safe investment. If the child dies, the property goes to his heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor; a child who is not yet halachically an adult
A safe, protected investment or holding set aside for someone
Heirs; the people who inherit someone's property

phrases.english: If he accepted a deposit from a minor –
he should make a safe investment for him,
and if the minor dies, he must return it to his heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of deposits from a woman and a slave on the previous daf, now covering a minor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deposit from a קטן is put into a safe investment for him; if he dies, it goes to his heirs.

steps.title: A dying person's claim that an item belongs to someone else
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if any of these people say before death that the item belongs to a certain person, we follow their words if believable. If not, we set their words aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of these people who said at the time of their death, 'These belong to so-and-so,' the guardian should do as they explained. And if not, he should give their explanation its own explanation, meaning he ignores what they said.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a rule for when one of these people says before dying, 'This item really belongs to someone else.' Sometimes we follow that statement, and sometimes we set it aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the item would go to the husband, the master, or the heirs. A deathbed statement saying 'it belongs to פלוני' would take it away from them. So we follow the statement only when it is believable; otherwise we 'explain their explanation', meaning we don't rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of their death; while they were dying
According to their explanation; as they said
An explanation of their explanation; setting aside what they said and not relying on it

steps.confusionAlert: 'יַעֲשֶׂה פֵּירוּשׁ לְפֵירוּשָׁן' sounds like 'explain it even more carefully.' It actually means the opposite: don't follow their words, and handle the item the normal way.

phrases.english: And all of them who said at the time of their death:
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the people in this ברייתא who gave deposits: the woman, the slave and the minor.

phrases.english: "These belong to so-and-so,"
he should act according to their explanation.
And if not, he should make an explanation of their explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a general rule that applies to all the depositors listed in the ברייתא, including the minor from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deathbed statement that an item belongs to someone else is followed only if it is believable; otherwise it is set aside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the story that follows, where רב applies this exact wording to a real case.

steps.title: רב's ruling about the rings of רבה בר בר חנה's wife
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה's wife said before dying that her rings belonged to מרתא and her daughter's sons. רב told him to follow her words only if he trusts her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of רבה בר בר חנה, when she was dying, said: 'These rings belong to מרתא and the sons of her daughter.' He came before רב. רב said to him: 'If she is trustworthy to you, do as she explained. And if not, make an explanation of her explanation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case that matches the ברייתא's rule. רב applies the ברייתא's wording: follow her statement only if her husband trusts her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As her husband, רבה בר בר חנה would normally inherit her rings. Her deathbed words would take them away from him and give them to others. רב makes it depend on whether he believes she was a truthful person. If he does, the rings go to מרתא and the grandsons; if not, he keeps them.

keyTerms.meaning: When she was lying on her deathbed; when she was dying

phrases.english: The wife of Rabba bar bar Chana,
when she was dying, said:
"These rings belong to Marta and the sons of her daughter."
He came before Rav, who said to him:
If she is trustworthy to you, act according to her explanation,
and if not, make an explanation of her explanation.
phrases.notes: Same phrase as in the ברייתא: don't follow her words, and as her heir, keep the rings.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, כִּי קָא שָׁכְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule from step 2 to a real case decided by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband follows his dying wife's statement only if he believes she is trustworthy.

steps.title: Another version: it depends on an estimate of her means
steps.stepSummary: A second version says רב told him to follow her words if he could judge that the rings were probably not hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say this is what רב said to him: 'If you can estimate it, do as she explained. And if not, make an explanation of her explanation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב's answer. Here the test is not her honesty but whether the facts make her claim likely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, everything depends on whether the husband trusts her as a person. In this version, it depends on his estimate of the situation, meaning whether it seems likely that the rings were deposited with her and were not her own. The final instruction is the same: follow her words when the test is met, and set them aside when it isn't.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say; introduces a second version of a statement
Estimated; judged by assessing the situation

steps.whatToRemember: A dying person's claim that 'this belongs to someone else' is followed only when it is believable. רב applies this in two versions: either it depends on trusting her as a person, or on estimating whether the rings were likely deposited with her.

phrases.english: And there are those who say this is what he said to him:
If you can estimate it, act according to her explanation,
phrases.notes: He means: if you can judge from the situation that the rings were likely deposited with her and weren't really hers.

phrases.english: and if not, make an explanation of her explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב's ruling from step 3, changing the test from personal trust to an estimate of the facts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband follows his wife's statement if he can judge that the rings were likely deposited with her; otherwise he sets it aside.

steps.title: What is a 'safe investment' for a minor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's words about a קטן's deposit and asks what 'סגולה' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that if the guardian took the deposit from a minor, he must make a 'סגולה' for him. What is a 'סגולה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase from the ברייתא and asks what it means in practice. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 told us the guardian must invest the קטן's money safely, but it never said in what. Here the גמרא wants a concrete example of a lasting, safe investment.

keyTerms.meaning: A safe, lasting investment or asset

phrases.english: From a minor, he must make a safe investment for him.
What is a 'safe investment'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Step 1 to explain one of its words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of asset counts as a 'סגולה' for a minor's money.

steps.title: A Torah scroll or a date palm
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a ספר תורה. רבה בר רב הונא says a date palm that produces fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: a ספר תורה. רבה בר רב הונא said: a date palm from which he will eat dates.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each give an example of a safe investment for the קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא picks a ספר תורה, a valuable item that holds its worth and is also a מצוה. רבה בר רב הונא picks a date palm, which keeps its value and also gives the child produce to eat.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: A Torah scroll.
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
A date palm, from which he will eat dates.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סגולה is either a ספר תורה (רב חסדא) or a fruit-bearing date palm (רבה בר רב הונא).

steps.title: Father and son: even after splitting, no חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a father and son cannot make a חזקה on each other's property. רב יוסף says this is true even if they split their finances.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a father has no חזקה in his son's property, and a son has none in his father's property. רב יוסף said: even if they split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list of people who cannot make a חזקה, and רב יוסף says how far the rule reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, using a field for three years creates a חזקה, a presumption that you own it. A father and son don't make one, because they freely use each other's things. רב יוסף says that even after they separate their money, the rule stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption of ownership based on using property for some time

phrases.english: And a father does not have a חזקה in his son's property,
and a son does not have one in his father's property.
Rav Yosef said: Even if they split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף, a father and son cannot make a חזקה on each other's property even after they split.

steps.title: רבא: after splitting, the rule no longer applies
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: once they have split, they can make a חזקה like anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if they split, the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view from רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the reason there is no חזקה is that they share things. Once their money is separate, that reason is gone, so a חזקה works as usual.

keyTerms.meaning: Not; here, the rule does not apply

phrases.english: Rava said: If they split, the rule does not apply.
phrases.notes: 'לא' means the 'no חזקה' rule stops. They can now make a חזקה like strangers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב יוסף from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבא, after a father and son split, each can make a חזקה on the other's property.

steps.title: A real court case followed רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדפתי reports that רב פפי ruled in an actual case like רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדפתי said: רב פפי ruled in a real case that 'if they split, the rule does not apply,' like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבא from a real ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge actually deciding a case this way carries real weight. It shows רבא's view was followed in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case, a practical ruling

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
Rav Pappi ruled in a real case:
'If they split, the rule does not apply,' like Rava.

steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that after splitting there can be a חזקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practical ruling by רב פפי.

steps.title: A chain of tradition also says like רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק passes on, through several people, that רב נחמן בר יעקב also said 'if they split, the rule does not apply.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רב חייא from הורמיז ארדשיר told me that רב אחא בר יעקב told him in the name of רב נחמן בר יעקב: if they split, the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: A second source backs רבא, this time a tradition passed down from an earlier teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is both a practical ruling and a tradition from רב נחמן בר יעקב on רבא's side. The long chain of names shows exactly how the teaching was passed along.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתַּעִי לִי רַב חִיָּיא מֵהוֹרְמִיז אַרְדְּשִׁיר,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya from Hurmiz Ardeshir told me

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִישְׁתַּעִי לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: that Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov told him
in the name of Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov:
If they split, the rule does not apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support for רבא after the court case in Step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition from רב נחמן בר יעקב.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules: if they split, the rule does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: if they split, the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling in favor of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father and son who have separated their finances are treated like strangers. Each of them can make a חזקה on the other's property.
steps.whatToRemember: Father and son who live together cannot make a חזקה on each other's property. Once they split their finances, they can.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: If they split, the rule does not apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between רב יוסף and רבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבא: after splitting, a father and son can make a חזקה on each other's property.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a son who split and a wife who was divorced are like everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: a son who split off, and a wife who was divorced, are like all other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the ruling it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the son who split next to a divorced wife. Once the close relationship that let them use each other's things is over, they are treated like strangers for חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
A son who split off, and a wife who was divorced,
are like all other people.

steps.raayaObject: The הלכה that after splitting there can be a חזקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a son who split and a divorced wife.

steps.title: The brother who ran the business: רב says he must prove it
steps.stepSummary: One brother managed the family business and the documents carry his name. He claims the assets came from his mother's father. רב says he must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one of the brothers was doing business for the household, and sale documents and loan documents went out in his name. He said: 'They are mine, they came to me from my mother's father's family.' רב said: he must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: A new case is introduced, and רב gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he was running the shared family business, documents in his name could easily be family money. So רב puts the burden of proof on him, and otherwise the assets are shared among all the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (a dispute between אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated: One of the brothers
who was doing business for the household,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ אוֹנוֹת וּשְׁטָרוֹת יוֹצְאִין עַל שְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: and sale documents and other documents were going out in his name,
and he said: They are mine,
for they came to me from my mother's father's family.
Rav said: He must bring proof.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the brother claiming the assets as his own must prove it.

steps.title: שמואל: the brothers must prove it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the other brothers must bring proof that the assets are family property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the brothers must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב about who must prove the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, documents in this brother's name count in his favor. So the other brothers must show that the money really belonged to their father.

keyTerms.meaning: On the brothers (they carry the burden)

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עַל הָאַחִין לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: The brothers must bring proof.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the other brothers must prove the assets belong to the family.

steps.title: שמואל: רב agrees if the brother died
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רב would agree that if the brother who held the documents died, the brothers must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: אבא (רב) agrees with me that if he died, the brothers must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל points out a case where even רב would agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the brother has died, his heirs cannot know where the money came from. They keep the assets unless the other brothers prove otherwise.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל argue over who must prove ownership while the brother is alive. Once he has died, both agree the other brothers must bring proof.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Abba agrees with me
phrases.notes: 'אבא' here is רב. That was his actual name.

phrases.english: that if he died,
the brothers must bring proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the argument of Steps 13 and 14 by naming a case where both agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the brother died, everyone agrees the other brothers must bring proof.

steps.title: רב פפא: Orphans get no stronger claim than their father
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges שמואל: since the father himself would have needed proof according to רב, how can his orphans be in a better position?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: Do we make claims for orphans that their father could not have made for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks שמואל's last statement from Step 15. He asks how orphans can win with a claim their own father could not have used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the brother who managed the business had to bring proof that the assets came from his mother's father. So if he had lived, his claim alone would not have helped him. רב פפא argues that his orphans should not get a better legal position than he had, so רב should not agree that the brothers must bring proof after he dies.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
We argue (make a claim on someone's behalf)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule that בית דין argues on behalf of orphans (טוענין ליתומים) is real. רב פפא is limiting it: בית דין only raises claims the father himself could have raised.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it:
phrases.notes: He's pushing back on שמואל's claim in Step 15 that רב would agree once the brother died.

phrases.english: Do we make claims for orphans
something that their father could not claim for them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges שמואל's statement in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רב agrees the brothers must bring proof once the document-holder has died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Orphans inherit their father's legal position. If the father needed proof according to רב, the orphans cannot be exempt from proof.

steps.title: רבא took lent-type items from orphans without proof
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא backs up his objection with a case where רבא took scissors and a book from orphans without requiring proof, because such items are commonly lent out.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, רבא took a pair of garment scissors and a book of אגדה away from orphans without requiring proof, since these are things people usually lend and rent out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a real ruling of רבא to prove that orphans get no special protection beyond what their father had. The sentence ends with a dash because the argument continues into the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone holding an item is believed that it is his. But for items that are commonly lent or rented, holding them proves nothing, even for the father. Since רבא did not argue for the orphans that the items belonged to their father, this shows we do not argue for orphans what the father himself could not claim.

keyTerms.meaning: He took out (removed from someone's possession)
A pair of scissors used for cutting garments
Items that are commonly lent and rented out

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle that holding a commonly lent item does not count as evidence of ownership, and that orphans cannot rely on it either.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava take away
a pair of garment scissors and a book of aggada
from orphans, without proof,
phrases.notes: The person asking for the items back did not have to prove they were his.

phrases.english: in the case of items that are commonly lent and rented out –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the supporting source for רב פפא's challenge in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's principle that we do not argue for orphans what their father could not have argued.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling taking commonly lent items from orphans without requiring proof.
